_note: Voiceover text for ElevenLabs, one clip per scene. Numbers are spelled out so they are read naturally. Run: npm run voiceover

scenes.text: If you work in compliance at a UK lender, you'll know the feeling. Every week the FCA, the PRA and the ICO publish more than anyone can read properly. Someone still has to decide what actually matters for your firm. Usually by hand, in a spreadsheet.

This is RegPulse. I've given it a sample firm, Northbridge Business Finance, a small lender in Manchester. It knows Northbridge's fifteen policies and process maps, who owns each one, and the controls inside them.

When I run a sweep, Tavily searches the regulators' websites for the dates I choose and brings back clean text. Then a small, fast model, Nemotron Nano, reads every publication and asks one question. Does this apply to us? Fund rules, crypto, and anything that's PRA only, drop out straight away. Six of the eleven go through.
Those six go to Nemotron Ultra, which reads each one against the whole policy library. And this is what comes back. Fourteen changes, two of them high priority, each with an owner and a date.

Here's the one I'd look at first. The FCA has restricted six unregulated lenders over money laundering. Nothing to do with Northbridge, you'd think. But the same press release reminds regulated firms to check the registration of the Annex 1 firms they deal with. Some of Northbridge's introducers are exactly that. RegPulse found the open audit point in the introducer policy, and put the regulator's own words right next to it.
Every finding has to quote the source word for word. If the quote isn't really there, the finding is thrown away. You can't act on a rule that doesn't exist.
From here I can draft the change ticket. A user story with acceptance criteria, ready for Jira, or a Pega case. Or I can just ask a question, and the answer comes back with its sources.

That whole sweep took thirty-three seconds and cost about eight cents on Nebius Token Factory. Sending the triage to Nano instead of Ultra cut that step's cost by ninety-three percent. It's open source, and you can point it at your own policies. RegPulse. So the one rule that matters doesn't get lost in the pile.
